content: 1. Norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol monophasic kits are prescribed as follows: one active tablet is taken orally once daily for days 1 through 21, followed by one inert tablet daily (or no tablets) for days 22 through 28. After this, a new pill pack is started. For multiphasic, biphasic, or triphasic dosing, refer to the manufacturer’s package insert and follow the color-coded sequence provided. Blood pressure should be monitored during use, and caution is advised. This medication is not recommended for premenarcheal individuals. 2. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of fezolinetant by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Co-administration with weak, moderate, or strong CYP1A2 inhibitors increases fezolinetant’s AUC and peak plasma concentration. 3. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 4. Co-administration of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir with ethinyl estradiol is contraindicated due to an unspecified interaction mechanism. This combination may increase the toxicity of either drug. Clinical trials have shown ALT elevations greater than five times the upper limit of normal (ULN), with some cases exceeding 20 times ULN, when ethinyl estradiol is co-administered with these drugs. Ethinyl estradiol-containing medications should be discontinued before starting this hepatitis C combination regimen and restarted approximately two weeks after completing the regimen. 5. Acitretin decreases the effects of norethindrone through an unknown mechanism. This combination is contraindicated, as it may result in contraceptive failure. 6. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered, as hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 7. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of anastrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Anastrozole should not be used concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. Alternative drugs should be considered. 8. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, can lower the exposure of CYP3A4 substrates. Alternative drugs should be used when possible, and therapeutic effects should be monitored if co-administration is unavoidable. 9. Armodafinil decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 10. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration may lead to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Women of reproductive potential should use effective nonhormonal contraception. Based on animal studies, belzutifan may cause fetal harm. 11. Atazanavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when co-administered with ethinyl estradiol. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 12. Brigatinib decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with hormonal contraceptives may result in decreased concentrations and loss of efficacy. Brigatinib may cause fetal harm. Women should use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for at least four months after the last dose. 13. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 14. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control when co-administered. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 15. Calaspargase pegol may indirectly interact with oral contraceptives, and concomitant use is not recommended. Non-oral contraceptive methods should be used for females of childbearing potential. 16. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of heparin and enoxaparin through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. This combination is contraindicated. 17. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A substrates should be avoided. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 18. Indinavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when co-administered with ethinyl estradiol. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 19. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be avoided. If unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic effect. 20. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 21. Leniolisib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase systemic exposure to BCRP substrates, including ethinyl estradiol. Alternative drugs should be considered. 22. Lesinurad decreases the effects of norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control when co-administered. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 23. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of letrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Letrozole should not be used concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 24. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of fedratinib, a CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 substrate. Co-administration with dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors should be avoided. 25. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic enzymes CYP3A4 and CYP2E1 metabolism. Co-administration may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. Alternative drugs should be considered. 26. Fosamprenavir may alter hormone levels when co-administered with ethinyl estradiol, potentially reducing virologic response. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 27. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control when co-administered. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 28. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended.
